children: Technology real estate company Offerpad (NYSE:OPAD)will be reporting earnings this Monday after the bell. Here’s what to look for.

Offerpad missed analysts’ revenue expectations last quarter, reporting revenues of $77.65 million, down 51.6% year on year. It was a disappointing quarter for the company, with revenue guidance for next quarter missing analysts’ expectations significantly and a significant miss of analysts’ EPS estimates. It reported 206 homes sold, down 54.4% year on year.
Is Offerpad a buy or sell going into earnings?

params.linkText: Read our full analysis here, it’s free for active Edge members

children: This quarter, the market is expecting Offerpad’s revenue to decline 18.4% year on year, improving from the 36.2% decrease it recorded in the same quarter last year.

Analysts covering the company have generally reconfirmed their estimates over the last 30 days, suggesting they anticipate the business will stay the course heading into earnings. Offerpad has missed Wall Street’s revenue estimates multiple times over the last two years.

Looking at Offerpad’s peers in the consumer discretionary - real estate services segment, some have already reported their Q3 results, giving us a hint as to what we can expect. JLL delivered year-on-year revenue growth of 11.8%, beating analysts’ expectations by 1.5%, and Newmark reported revenues up 12.7%, topping estimates by 2.2%. JLL traded up 17.9% following the results while Newmark was down 4.5%.

There has been positive sentiment among investors in the consumer discretionary - real estate services segment, with share prices up 3.2% on average over the last month. Offerpad is down 33.5% during the same time and is heading into earnings with an average analyst price target of $12.25 (compared to the current share price of $2.17).
